::: {.why}
You will be shown C++ in an interview and you will want to read exchange and engine code, and reading is a far smaller skill than writing, which is what this week targets.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Read a short C++ function and say what is copied, what is referenced and what is moved.
- State what the compilation model does that Python's does not, and what that buys.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Work through LearnCpp's chapters on fundamental types, references and pointers, and const. The three ideas you need are that objects have declared types known at compile time, that a reference is an alias rather than a pointer, and that const is part of the type.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Read and annotate: take twenty lines of real C++ from the LEAN engine or any open source order book, and annotate every line with what is copied and what is referenced. Getting this right is most of what reading C++ requires.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Twenty lines of real C++ annotated line by line with what is copied, referenced and moved.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Given a function signature taking a const reference, say what that guarantees the function will and will not do.
:::
